sections.content: How many people are "sales accounts and business development managers"?

282,165 people

were counted on the census as "sales accounts and business development managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Sales accounts and business development managers organise and carry out market research to meet the requirements of an organisation�s marketing and sales policies.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "sales accounts and business development managers", 16.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sales accounts and business development managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sales accounts and business development managers" included:

  • early education and childcare services managers
  • occupational therapists
  • hairdressing and beauty salon managers and proprietors

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sales accounts and business development managers" there were more men than women (61.5% compared with 38.5%).

This means "sales accounts and business development managers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 61.5% and women made up 38.5% of "sales accounts and business development managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sales accounts and business development managers" included:

  • management consultants and business analysts
  • assemblers (electrical and electronic products)
  • functional managers and directors (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sales accounts and business development managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "sales accounts and business development managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sales accounts and business development managers", 5.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (91.4% compared with 8.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.1%) than self-employed (2.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
